fact: Prime Minister Russell Dlamini's first-quarter 2026/27 report to Parliament said Cabinet approved the National Payment Systems Regulations of 2026; the story gives no gazette publication or start date, so they are recorded as not yet shown in force (date is the story's publication date, 2026-07-23).

The National Payments System Act, 2023 (Act No. 5 of 2023) was enacted by the King and Parliament; it regulates payment systems and payment service providers and repeals the National Clearing and Settlement Systems Act No. 17 of 2011 (no commencement date in the passages; document published 2023-01-01 used as date).

The Central Bank of Eswatini's payments deputy director said the National Payment Systems Act of 2023 sets the bank's powers and the obligations of payment system providers and participants, and that licensing runs now under the bank's mobile money guidelines while detailed regulations are being finalised.
The Central Bank of Eswatini said it is finalising regulations under the National Payment Systems Act that spell out licensing timelines, documentation and detailed requirements.

The article names three mobile money operators, including MTN MoMo and Instacash, in the interoperable system and the central bank says a new mobile money provider must go through its licensing process, with non-bank providers driving most financial inclusion gains.

fact: The Central Bank of Eswatini Governor said, at the 11 December 2024 launch of Fast Payments on the Eswatini Payment Switch, that participation is mandated for all payment service providers offering local payments, with the remaining participants expected to be live by the end of January 2025 (BIS Review published the speech 2025-01-14).

fact: The Central Bank of Eswatini issued the CMA EFT Payments Directive no 1 of 2025 under the National Payments System Act, 2023, binding all payment service providers from 31 March 2025.
The directive defines payment service providers as persons or institutions licensed under section 22 of the National Payments System Act, 2023.
The directive sets a regulator deadline of 31 March 2027 for payment service providers to migrate low-value CMA cross-border transfers from SADC-RTGS to the TCIB scheme.
